verdict.rationale: Angular ships first-party SSR (Angular Universal / @angular/ssr) and a first-party router directly inside the core framework, and community evidence confirms production use of prerendering for SPAs, which covers much of the full-stack routing/data-fetching need. However, unlike React's Next.js or Vue's Nuxt, there is no distinct official meta-framework product built on top of Angular; SSR/routing are folded into the core platform itself. Missing for 10: a standalone official meta-framework product analogous to Next.js/Nuxt/SvelteKit, first-party docs framing SSR+routing as a separate meta-framework layer, and independent hands-on confirmation of such a distinct product.
